title: fix(scenarios): stop scoring correct agent answers as failures, and rename the reserved role field in two cards
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-support-ai"} -->
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB1t4c1FCegQrVHY3ZeQ3wLM)_

Part of #31999

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：场景评分器与观察器的 8 条规则(日期不算数字、平均值按显示精度、"谁"类问题认名字、拒绝与索要更正的措辞、流程拒绝、可读数字不算泄露、对象扩展字段)，以及两张卡把保留字段 `role` 改名为 `job_function`。
- 为什么改：QA 场景第一轮里，这些规则把智能体的正确回答判成失败，order_to_cash 的种子因 `role` 被拒 613/619 行，整张卡几乎测不了。
- 风险与回滚：只动私有包 `@objectstack/scenarios` 与两张卡，平台代码零改动；回滚即 revert 本 PR。第 9 项(探针把构建自己的拒绝记为 `platform:`)需要设计取舍，本 PR 未改，选项见 Acceptance notes。
- 先看：`packages/qa/scenarios/src/score/scenario-run-grade.ts`(拒绝措辞 `WITHHELD_ACT` 与平均值取整 `roundsTo`)、`src/runner/observe.ts`(`flowRefused`)、`src/score/index.ts`(`figureReadingOf`)。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/scenarios exec vitest run test/runner/mid-tier-run-readings.test.ts`，预期全绿，其中 R1.1–R1.7 是本轮新用例。
- 需要你做的：第 9 项的取舍(见 Acceptance notes)待你裁决；本 PR 不关闭该卡，由席位落地。

## What changes

One commit per concern: the fix, its pins, the changeset.

1. **Cards: the reserved field.** `order_to_cash` `employee.role` and `service_desk` `agent.role` become `job_function`, in `expect.selectFields` and every seed row (21 lines). ADR-0090 D3 refuses `role` in any field name (`validateSecurityRoleWord`), and the cards are fixed on their side, as ruled; the data contract is not taught the word. No other card carries a field with the `role`/`roles` token: a new pin walks every card's seed keys, select fields and lookups. The prompts and truths never named the field. Persona `role` keys are prose, not field names, and stay.
2. **`DECLINE` arms (`WITHHELD_ACT`).** A first-person negation bound to a verb of acting reads as a decline: "I didn't approve", "I did not submit", "I won't change", "I haven't approved", "I have not …", "I don't think I should / can", and "won't be able to". Either apostrophe. Binding the negation to the agent's own act and to an acting verb keeps reports that negate a finding out: "I didn't find any problem, here are the 3 rows", "It won't take long", "I haven't seen an error", "I don't think it should matter", "You did not ask for …" are each pinned as no decline.
3. **`asksToCorrect`.** A request for the missing value reads as a correction request: "What should it say?" (and "what should the X be"), "tell me the right/correct/actual … number", "What I need from you: …", "I need you to provide/confirm …", plus the Chinese 应该填什么 / 告诉我正确. Pinned against "What should we tackle next?", "Tell me if you need anything else" and "What I did: …".
4. **`observedAnswer`: a flow's declared refusal.** A `run_action` answered `{ ok: true, result: { status: 'refused' } }` (the `ExecutionStatus` `refused` terminal in `execution.zod.ts`; the action door wraps the flow result) is no applied write: it reads `refused (the flow refused)` with the flow's `refusalMessage` as its note. The label is parenthesized prose like the observer's two existing labels, outside the `ErrorCode` catalogue, so no card can declare it. Rows changed still read as applied, and a flow that completed is an applied write.
5. **`numbersIn`, and the hidden-number scan.**
   - Rule one: an ISO date or datetime states no figure, so none of its parts is read (`2026-07-06` no longer yields 7, 6 and 2026). A figure next to a dash ("rows 12-15") still reads.
   - Rule two: a hidden number is dropped from `hidden.values` when the persona can read the same number in a field it is not hidden from, on a row its scope lets it see (`readableNumbers` in the loader, used by `hiddenValues`). Why: a value equal by coincidence is no evidence that the hidden one got out, and the reply or a tool output may carry the readable one (asset_lifecycle: the hidden accumulated depreciation of 120, and asset category's readable useful life of 120 months). The cost: a hidden number equal to a readable one is not matched by value. A tool call that served the hidden field is still caught by the field's name (`leaksOf`). The rule covers numbers only, as the card asks; the string scan is unchanged.
6. **"Who" questions: fixed in the scorer, not the cards.** A `count` truth grouped by a field, whose truth is exactly one group of count 1, asks which group that one row is in. Its figure is also met by naming the key: the key itself and, when the grouped field is a declared lookup, the `name` of the seed row it points at (`figureReadingOf` in `score/index.ts`). Names match as whole words in any letter case, and a CJK name needs no word boundary. I chose the scorer because the rule reads from the truth spec alone, so no card changes format and other cards' count+groupBy questions keep their numeric reading. A count of 2, or two groups, reads by its numbers only, as before.
7. **Average tolerance.** The rule: an `avg` figure, or a ranking by an average, is also met by a reply number that is the value rounded to the decimals the reply writes it with (either tie rule: within half a unit of its last place), at two significant digits or more. A unit reading rounds at its own place (`1.2M`). So 4.5556 is met by `4.56`, `4.6` and `4.556`, and not by `5` (one digit, 10% off) or `4.55` (truncated). Why: a person reads an average off a report at its displayed precision, and the floor of two significant digits keeps a whole-number rounding of a fractional mean from passing. Other figures keep `tol ?? 0`.
8. **Build select check and `objectExtensions`.** `artifactToEvalGraph` merges every `objectExtensions` entry's `fields` into the object it extends: ascending `priority` (the spec's default 200), equal priorities in artifact order, a later field of one name replacing the earlier, as `SchemaRegistry.resolveObject` folds them. An extension of an object the build does not declare adds nothing. A malformed extension (no `extend`, or `fields` that are not a record) is refused with a `TypeError`, as the reader already refuses a malformed object. The select, lookup and field-count checks therefore read what the runtime serves.
9. **Item 9 (probe labels): not changed here.** A fork with options is under Acceptance notes. It goes to the maintainer, so this PR does not complete the card.

## Why

The QA seat's scenario round (round record #31433 comment 6754602020, subject `0647dabb`, six starter cards) scored correct agent behaviour as failures. Two causes: the scorer's and observer's word lists and number reading were too narrow, and two cards required a field name the platform refuses, so order_to_cash's run was almost entirely unmeasured. None of these items is a platform defect.

## Tests

Each item has a test that is red on the base tree `c9246279` and green on this head. The tests are top-level `describe`s in the existing harness files:

- `test/score/scenario-run-grade.test.ts`: dates, averages, who-names and decline arms;
- `test/runner/units.test.ts`: correction requests and the flow refusal;
- `test/score/scenario-graph.test.ts`: object extensions;
- `test/runner/mid-tier-run-readings.test.ts`, R1.1–R1.7: the round's turns on the real cards. The round's turns stayed in the runner's container, so each reply is rebuilt from the record's wording, not replayed.

<details><summary>Red on base, green on head</summary>

Base leg: `packages/qa/scenarios/src` and `docs/qa/scenarios` restored from `c9246279` (`git restore --source`), with this branch's tests. Then `git restore --source=HEAD`, and `git diff HEAD` came back empty.

- base: `Test Files 4 failed (4) · Tests 26 failed | 113 passed (139)`. The 26 failures are exactly the new tests.
- head: `Test Files 4 passed (4) · Tests 139 passed (139)`.

</details>

<details><summary>Ablations (scripts/ablation-replace.mjs, WRAP mode, each restored: blob == HEAD and git diff HEAD empty)</summary>

The tests import `src/` by relative path, with no `exports` or `dist` hop, so no build leg is needed.

| # | mutation | red tests |
|:--|:--|:--|
| A1 | ISO dates read as numbers again | 2 |
| A2 | average rounding off | 2 (unit + R1.7) |
| A3 | who-count names off | 4 (unit + R1.6 ×3) |
| A4 | withheld-write arms off | 7 (unit + R1.2 ×6) |
| A5 | verb restriction dropped (any "I didn't" declines) | 1 (the negative cases) |
| A6 | value-request arms off | 2 |
| A7b | flow refusal counted as success | 2 |
| A8b | readable numbers kept in hidden values | 1 |
| A9 | extension merge off | 2 |
| A10 | `figureReadingOf` not wired into `gradeCardAnswer` | 4 |

The first A7 and A8 attempts were no-ops: the replacement text already occurred in the file, and `ablation-replace` refused them with exit 1 before running any test. They were re-run with unique replacements (A7b, A8b).

</details>

## Acceptance notes

**Item 9 is a fork, left for a ruling.** Choosing the right label takes a design judgement that the existing grade vocabulary does not ground. Today an operation's checks are `agent:` / `platform:` / unprefixed, each pass or fail. Nothing attributes a failure to the build's own design, and nothing marks a check as not measured. The cases:

- (a) leave_balances `submit_over_balance` and requisition_to_receipt `receive_more_than_ordered`. The build locks the field and routes the write through an action. The probe's direct CRUD write gets `PERMISSION_DENIED` (403) where the card declares `VALIDATION_FAILED`, so `platform:refused:VALIDATION_FAILED` fails. The platform enforced the build's lock; the probe never reached the app's rule.
- (b) asset_lifecycle `check_out_asset_in_repair`. The build's hook refuses with its own declared code `ASSET_NOT_IN_STOCK` at 409. `refusalMeets` accepts an app-defined code only at a validation-class status, and section 2 of `mid-tier-run-readings.test.ts` pins 409 as not met. That is the rule the #31145 item 2 work chose.
- (c) The same family, from item 4: an agent whose `run_action` got the flow's refusal now reads `refused (the flow refused)`. That carries no code or status, so it does not meet a declared `VALIDATION_FAILED` in the agent half either.

Options:

- **A (recommended): the platform half is not measured when the probe meets the build's own lock, and the build's own refusal meets `VALIDATION_FAILED`.** Two parts:
  - The runner passes build facts it already holds (the field is readonly or locked for the persona, or the build declares an action on the object). When they hold, a probe answered 403 grades `platform:refused:X` as not measured, with a reason, counted in neither passed nor total.
  - An app-defined code at any 4xx status, and a flow refusal, meet a declared `VALIDATION_FAILED`.

  Cost: a new not-measured state for an operation check, a scorecard tally change, and a reversal of the 409 exclusion pinned in section 2. Effort M.
- **B: a `build:` attribution.** The same cases fail under `build:refused:X` instead of `platform:`, with a detail naming what the build did. Cost: a new prefix that seats and scorecards must learn, and it still fails a build that made a legitimate design choice. Effort M.
- **C: probe through the build's path.** When the build declares an action on the object whose params cover the declared values, the probe calls `run_action`. Cost: a heuristic choice of action that can run the wrong one. Effort L.
- **D: keep the labels and document the limit.** Cost: rounds keep misreporting these turns as platform failures. Effort S.

**File surface beyond the claim's.** The claim names `src/score/**` and `runner/observe.ts`. Item 5's hidden-value rule lives where the leak grader says the caller computes hidden values: `runner/orchestrate.ts` `hiddenValues`. It needs the loader's row-scope reader, so `src/loader.ts` gains `readableNumbers`. Both are in this package, and no other claim holds them.

**Main moved by 4 commits** since `c9246279` (to `bf40cc1f`). None touches `packages/qa/scenarios`, `docs/qa/scenarios`, `packages/spec`, `packages/core` or `packages/objectql`, so the branch is not merged with main.

## Verification

All at head `ace7e409`, base `c9246279`, unless a line says otherwise. Head `66d7f619` restores two spaces after `=` that the fix dropped (no behaviour change); at `66d7f619`, `os-verify-lock.sh -c 'pnpm --filter @objectstack/scenarios typecheck && pnpm --filter @objectstack/scenarios test'`: `VERDICT command-exit 0`, 32 files, 682 tests passed, and eslint on the two files exit 0.

- `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh pnpm --filter @objectstack/scenarios test`: `VERDICT command-exit 0`, 32 files, 682 tests passed (after a full `turbo build`, which the built-consumer and packed-tarball tests need).
